title: S01-03 - The Creature and Her Young

sections.title: Player text
sections.body: From behind the cart steps a large creature: the body of a wolf, the face of an owl, broad feathered wings folded along its back. It lifts its head from the meal and studies you, unhurried, deciding whether you are a threat. Then, behind it, two smaller shapes stumble into view: clumsy, big-eyed, and keeping close to its legs.

sections.title: Public objective
sections.body: Deal with the creature without anyone, including the pups, getting hurt, and clear the road.

Readaloud: From behind the cart steps a large creature: the body of a wolf, the face of an owl, broad feathered wings folded along its back. It lifts its head from the meal and studies you, unhurried, deciding whether you are a threat. Then, behind it, two smaller shapes stumble into view: clumsy, big-eyed, and keeping close to its legs.
Gmnotes: Player-safe: wary mother animal, two pups, road blocked by a decision. GM-only: she did not kill the driver; she is not manufactured.

Gmscript: Say: "She has not attacked. She is watching you and keeping herself between you and the young. If you want the name, locals call this kind of creature a strixwolf. The important part right now is not the name. It is her posture. What signal do you give her?"

Gmreadaloud: From behind the cart steps a large creature: wolf body, owl face, and broad feathered wings folded along her back. She studies you, unhurried, deciding whether you are a threat. Two smaller shapes stumble into view behind her, clumsy and big-eyed, keeping close to her legs.

Gmchecklist: Describe before naming. Introduce the pups before anyone commits to violence. Frame the creature as wary and protective, not aggressive. Hand the resolution to S01-04: Presence 10 to read and influence her.

Gmprivate: She is a natural preserve hybrid and a scavenger here, not the killer. If the party blames or kills her, the real killer's trail goes quieter and the corporate forest-danger story gets easier to believe.
Playertakeaway: You face a wary mother animal and two pups; your posture decides whether this turns violent.
Storytakeaway: The apparent monster is a parent protecting young, and the encounter is about restraint before violence.
Mechanictakeaway: The next roll reads intent and influences reaction: Presence against Difficulty 10, with mercy and aggression branching the scene.
